questions.question: 1. A 2-3 tree is a perfectly balanced binary search tree.

explanations.a: Correct. Every path from the root node to the leaf node has the same length in a 2-3 tree, making it a perfectly balanced tree.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A 2-3 tree is indeed a perfectly balanced binary search tree where all leaf nodes are at the same level.

questions.question: 2. Data items are arranged in a sorted order in a 2-3 tree. In a 3-node, the data item of the middle node is greater than the data item of the root node. What about the data item of the right node?

answers.a: Data item of right node is greater than root node but less than middle node
answers.b: Data item of right node is equal to both root node and middle node
answers.c: Data item of right node is greater than both root node and middle node
answers.d: Data item of right node is less than root node and middle node

explanations.a: Incorrect. This choice would make the 3-node unsorted. Data items less than the middle node should be on the left side, not the right side.
explanations.b: Incorrect. It is not necessary that the data item in the right node will always be equal to data items in the middle and root nodes.
explanations.c: Correct. The smallest data item is in the left node. The data item greater than the root node data item is in the middle node and the data item is greater than both the middle node data item and the root node data item is in the right node.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This choice would make the 3-node unsorted. A data item less than the root node data items should be placed in the left node.

questions.question: 3. Which of the following is the optimal data structure choice for implementation of searching operation?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Even though normal binary search trees have average lookup time complexity of O(log n), in worst cases it will increase to O(n) time complexity. Thus, they are not the most optimal choice of given options.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Even though treaps have average lookup time complexity of O(log n), in worst cases it will increase to O(n) time complexity. Thus, they are not the most optimal choice of given options.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The average lookup time complexity itself is O(n) in unordered lists. They are the worst of the given choices for implementation of searching operation.
explanations.d: Correct. Both the average case and worst case lookup time is O(log n) in 2-3 tree. Therefore, they are the best choice for implementation of searching operation.

questions.question: 4. What advantage do 2-3 trees have over normal binary search trees?

answers.a: Each node can have upto 3 children
answers.d: 2-3 trees do not have any advantage over binary search trees

explanations.a: Incorrect. Having upto 3 children alone does not grant any advantage to 2-3 trees over normal binary search trees.
explanations.b: Correct. 2-3 trees are always balanced in nature. Therefore, even in the worst case their height will be O(log n) compared to normal binary search trees whose height can increase to O(n) in worst cases. Moreover, this guarantees that the worst case time complexity for insertion, deletion, and searching will be O(log n) for 2-3 trees. Meanwhile for normal binary search tree worst case time complexity for insertion, deletion, and searching will be O(n).
explanations.c: Incorrect. Normal binary search trees can also have the leaf nodes at the same level. Moreover, just having leaf nodes at the same level does not offer any advantage to 2-3 trees.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 2-3 trees have significant advantages over binary search trees, particularly in maintaining balance.

questions.question: 5. Which of the following traversals would ensure that the elements are obtained in sorted order in a 2-3 tree?

explanations.a: Correct. Since the nodes are sorted in a 2-3 tree at every level, only inorder traversal would ensure that the obtained elements are in a sorted fashion.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Postorder traversal visits children before parents and doesn't produce sorted output in a 2-3 tree.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Preorder traversal visits parents before children and doesn't produce sorted output in a 2-3 tree.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Inorder traversal does produce sorted output in a 2-3 tree.

questions.question: 6. 2-3 trees provide better insertion than AVL trees.

explanations.a: Correct. Although the look-up complexity is the same as AVL trees, 2-3 trees provide better insertion performance because they require fewer rotations and rebalancing operations.
explanations.b: Incorrect. AVL trees take more time O(log n) to rebalance the tree for insertion compared to 2-3 trees which require fewer rebalancing operations.
